original_record.question: The diagram on the right shows nine points in a square array. What is the smallest number of points that need to be removed in order that no three of the remaining points are in a straight line? <image1>
original_record.solution: At least one point must be removed from each of the three horizontal lines; so at least three points need to be removed. However, removing the three points lying on either diagonal does what is required.
